- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2 price points above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model overestimates recovery — shift forecast downward by 3–5% of recent range.  
- Model often underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if recent 18-day mean is > 65, forecast should not drop below 62.  
- When sentiment is positive but forecast is falling, reverse the trend slightly — avoid “sentiment mismatch” by adding 1–2% to forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days.
